title: When your research agent sees a failed holdout, what happens to that test period?
author: Alphanet_dogwalker
selftext:
Reading the automated-research posts here got me thinking about what happens after a strategy fails its final test. 

Say an agent builds on 2020–2023, validates on 2024, then gets one look at 2025. It fails. You ask it to explain why, and that explanation goes into its research notes. Next week it proposes a different strategy using those notes. The new strategy hasn't directly queried 2025, but its design has already been influenced by what went wrong there. Starting a fresh chat wouldn't undo that if it can still read the notes.

For people actually running these loops, what do you do at that point? Move that period into development data and reserve a new test, keep the failure report away from the research agent, or freeze the revised strategy and wait for forward results?

I'm interested in a process that's workable after several failures. Keeping every test pristine sounds straightforward until you start running out of untouched history

comments.author: Exciting-World5861
comments.body: nothing happens to it, but you're right the more adjustments to the model it takes to get a good final test result, the less likely that performance will hold up on new unseen data. however any model that gets a good result on a sufficiently large test set has to have done that by successfully finding generalities from the training set. either way from a training point of view throwing away data is far worse than beginning to "overfit" your test data

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: The test period stops being a holdout the moment its result reaches the research notes, so I'd treat it as development data from then on. Keep a ledger of which periods were seen by which version of the agent. For the next test, use only forward data (new time that didn't exist when the strategy was designed), and write down the pass criteria and the number of attempts in advance. If you want to keep using a failure report, give the agent only a pass/fail flag and keep the explanation away from it. Since history runs out, count every failed attempt toward your trial total. Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source of data you could use to tag why a period failed without leaking it into the design.

comments.author: CODE_HEIST
comments.body:
even a pass/fail flag gives the next attempt information about that period. hiding the explanation limits the feedback, but doesn't make repeated tests independent.



i'd keep the failure for research, label that period as seen, and freeze both the next strategy and its pass criteria before collecting new forward results. also count abandoned attempts, not just the versions that reached a final report.
